ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: When an airplane changes from diving to pulling up, the pilot is in an overweight state. At this time, the supporting force of the seat on the pilot is greater than the gravity acting on the pilot. This phenomenon is called overload. Excessive overload will cause the pilot's limbs to be heavy, cerebral ischemia, temporary blindness, and even fainting. Specially trained air force pilots can withstand at most the effect of 9 times gravity. Take g as 10 m/s2. Then when the speed of the airplane diving and pulling up along a circular arc trajectory in a vertical plane is 100 m/s, the minimum radius of the circular arc trajectory is (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The problem gives: the pilot can withstand at most 9 times gravity, g=10 m/s^2, and the airplane speed v=100 m/s. When the airplane changes from diving to pulling up, the most dangerous position can be regarded as the lowest point of a vertical circular arc, and at this time the direction of centripetal acceleration is upward. Analyze the forces on the pilot: the seat supporting force N is upward, gravity mg is downward, satisfying N - mg = m v^2 / r. The overload not exceeding 9 times gravity means N <= 9mg. Therefore mg + m v^2 / r <= 9mg, simplifying gives v^2 / r <= 8g, so r >= v^2 / (8g). Substituting v=100 m/s and g=10 m/s^2 gives r_min = 100^2 / (8×10) = 10000 / 80 = 125 m.
